breakfast.name: Avocado on Toast
instructions: Toast sourdough until golden and crunchy
Mash avocado with lemon juice and salt
Spread thickly on toast
Top with pepper flakes, flaky salt
Add poached egg and crumbled feta if desired
breakfast.description: Yes, it's a global meme, but Australia really did start it — Melbourne cafés in the 2010s made it a worldwide phenomenon.

breakfast.name: Vegemite on Toast
instructions: Toast bread
Spread generously with butter while still hot
Apply a thin scrape of Vegemite — thick if you're brave
The butter must melt into the toast before the Vegemite goes on
breakfast.description: The national taste — salty, yeasty, polarizing. Australians learn to love it as children and defend it for life.

breakfast.name: Bacon and Egg Roll
instructions: Fry bacon until edges crisp
Fry eggs in bacon fat
Butter rolls
Stack bacon and egg in each roll
Add sauce — the 'barbie sauce vs tomato sauce' debate is ongoing
breakfast.description: The Saturday morning staple from every corner bakery and servo across the country.

lunch.name: Meat Pie
instructions: Brown mince with onion
Stir in flour, cook 1 min
Add stock, tomato paste, Worcestershire, Vegemite
Simmer 20 min until thick — filling should be saucy, not dry
Line pie tins with shortcrust, fill
Top with puff pastry, egg wash
Bake at 200°C for 25-30 min until puffed and golden
Eat with tomato sauce, ideally at the footy
lunch.description: Australia's unofficial national dish. Four'n Twenty pies outsell everything, but a good bakery pie is sacred.

lunch.name: Barramundi Fish and Chips
ingredients: Beer batter: 1 cup flour, 200ml cold beer, 1 egg, salt
instructions: Cut potatoes into thick chips, soak in water 30 min
Dry chips, fry at 140°C until soft, drain, then fry at 190°C until crispy
Make batter: whisk flour, beer, egg, salt — should be lumpy, not smooth
Pat fish dry, dust with flour
Dip in batter, lower into 190°C oil
Fry 4-5 min until deep golden
Drain, serve with chips, lemon, tartare
lunch.description: Barramundi is the quintessential Australian fish — firm, sweet, perfect for battering.

lunch.name: Chicken Parmigiana
instructions: Crumb chicken: flour, egg, breadcrumbs
Fry until golden both sides
Place on baking tray
Top with napolitana sauce, ham, mozzarella
Bake at 200°C until cheese melts and bubbles, 10-12 min
Serve with chips and garden salad — always
lunch.description: Every pub in Australia serves a parmi. The great 'parma vs parmi' pronunciation debate divides states.

dinner.name: BBQ Lamb Chops
instructions: Rub chops with oil, garlic, rosemary, salt, pepper
Get the barbie screaming hot
Grill 3-4 min per side for medium — Australians like them pink
Rest 5 min
Serve with mint sauce and roast vegetables
dinner.description: The Australian BBQ is backyard culture. Lamb chops are the weeknight default.

dinner.name: Roast Lamb Leg with Gravy
instructions: Stud lamb leg with garlic slivers and rosemary
Rub with oil, salt heavily
Roast at 220°C for 20 min, then 160°C for 90 min
Add potatoes and carrots around the lamb at the hour mark
Rest lamb 20 min, tented in foil
Make gravy from pan drippings: add flour, stir, add stock, simmer
Carve and serve with roast vegetables and gravy
dinner.description: The Australian Sunday roast — lamb outsells beef here. Leftovers become Monday's lamb sandwiches.

dinner.name: Kangaroo Steak with Native Pepperberry
ingredients: Native pepperberry (or black pepper and juniper)
Red wine jus: 200ml red wine, 200ml beef stock, butter
instructions: Bring steaks to room temperature
Season with salt, crushed pepperberry, garlic
Sear in very hot pan 2 min per side — kangaroo MUST be rare to medium-rare, it toughens when overcooked
Rest 5 min
Deglaze pan with red wine, reduce by half
Add stock, reduce, mount with butter
Slice against grain, serve over sweet potato mash with jus
dinner.description: Lean, gamey, and sustainably harvested — kangaroo is gaining pride of place on modern Australian menus.

snacks.name: Sausage Sizzle
instructions: Cook sausages on flat BBQ plate — snags should be brown all over
Slowly caramelize sliced onions in butter on same plate
Place sausage diagonally on a slice of white bread
Top with onions
Add tomato sauce — diagonal stripe, naturally
Fold bread over and eat with one hand
snacks.description: The Bunnings sausage sizzle: cheap white bread, a snag, onions, and sauce. Found outside every hardware store on weekends.

snacks.name: Damper (Bush Bread)
instructions: Mix flour and salt, rub in butter
Add milk, stir to sticky dough — don't overwork
Shape into round loaf on floured tray
Score a cross on top
Bake at 200°C for 25-30 min until hollow-sounding when tapped
Tear chunks and eat with butter or golden syrup
snacks.description: Bush bread from the droving days — stockmen baked it in campfire ashes. Still made at every school camp.

snacks.name: Fairy Bread
ingredients: Hundreds and thousands (round rainbow sprinkles — NOT jimmies or nonpareils)
instructions: Butter each slice of bread generously
Press buttered side firmly into a plate of hundreds and thousands
The sprinkles must be the round type — this is non-negotiable in Australia
Cut diagonally into triangles
Serve on a platter — no one takes just one
snacks.description: Buttered white bread covered in rainbow sprinkles — Australia's most beloved party food. Every child's birthday has it. Went viral globally when non-Australians discovered adults eat it too. The simplicity IS the point.

snacks.name: Chicken Salt Chips
ingredients: Chicken salt (a bright yellow seasoned salt — not actual chicken, it's a uniquely Australian spice blend of garlic, onion, paprika, and chicken flavoring)
instructions: Fry chips until golden and crispy
Toss immediately with chicken salt while hot — be generous
Serve in paper, standing up, at the beach or the footy
snacks.description: Hot chips dusted with chicken salt — a uniquely Australian obsession. The bright yellow seasoning went viral when the rest of the world realized Australia has its own chip seasoning and it's on everything.

snacks.name: Tim Tam Slam
instructions: Bite off both diagonal corners of the Tim Tam
Use the Tim Tam as a straw — suck hot drink through it
The hot liquid melts the chocolate interior into a molten mess
When you feel it start to collapse, shove the entire thing in your mouth
The result is a warm, melting, collapsing chocolate bomb
snacks.description: The Tim Tam Slam — using Australia's iconic chocolate biscuit as a straw for hot drinks. Went massively viral worldwide. The 2-second window between 'perfectly melted' and 'collapsed into your mug' is the thrill.

desserts.name: Pavlova
instructions: Beat egg whites to stiff peaks
Add sugar gradually, beating until glossy and thick
Fold in vinegar, cornflour, vanilla
Shape into round on lined tray — crater the center slightly
Bake at 120°C for 90 min, then turn off oven and leave inside to cool completely
Top with whipped cream
Pile with passionfruit pulp, sliced strawberries, kiwi
desserts.description: Named for ballerina Anna Pavlova. Australia and New Zealand both claim it — the rivalry is real and ongoing.

desserts.name: Lamingtons
ingredients: Sponge: 4 eggs, ¾ cup sugar, 1 cup flour, butter, milk
Chocolate icing: 3 cups icing sugar, ⅓ cup cocoa, 50g butter, ½ cup milk
instructions: Make vanilla sponge, bake at 180°C in square tin
Cool completely, refrigerate overnight for easier cutting
Cut into cubes (about 5cm)
Make chocolate icing: mix icing sugar, cocoa, melted butter, warm milk until smooth and runny
Dip each cube in chocolate using two forks
Roll immediately in coconut
Set on wire rack to dry
desserts.description: The iconic Australian cake — sponge cubes dipped in chocolate and rolled in coconut. January 21st is National Lamington Day.

desserts.name: Golden Gaytime Ice Cream Crumble
ingredients: 6 Golden Gaytime ice cream bars (toffee and vanilla ice cream, honeycomb biscuit crumbs)
instructions: Chop Golden Gaytime bars into chunks
Layer in serving glasses: ice cream chunks, cream, caramel, biscuit crumbs
Repeat layers
Top with extra honeycomb crumbs from the Gaytime coating
Serve immediately — it melts fast
desserts.description: Golden Gaytime — Australia's cult-favorite ice cream bar, deconstructed into a dessert. The honeycomb biscuit coating is the viral element. 'You can't have a Gaytime on your own' is the actual slogan.

drinks.name: Flat White
ingredients: Steamed milk (less foam than a latte, microfoam only)
instructions: Pull a double espresso into a ceramic cup
Steam milk to create velvety microfoam — less airy than a cappuccino, silkier than a latte
Pour milk over espresso, creating a thin layer of microfoam on top
No latte art mountains — just a flat, white surface of microfoam
drinks.description: Born in 1980s Australia (or New Zealand — another dispute). Stronger and less milky than a latte, now a worldwide staple.

drinks.name: Lemon, Lime and Bitters
instructions: Fill glass with ice
Dash Angostura bitters, swirl to coat glass
Add a splash of lime cordial
Top with lemonade
Garnish with lime slice
drinks.description: The non-alcoholic pub classic — every Australian kid grew up ordering an LLB at the bar.
